CX generated-code/runtime ABI ​

The generated C ABI is experimental. CX has not had a release and does not yet promise binary compatibility between releases. The current ABI version is 1. It identifies the C calling conventions, runtime entry points, runtime type layouts, interface reference representation, reflection layouts, object vtable, and value boxing helpers exposed through cx.h and generated project headers.

Runtime ABI checks are implemented in platform/common/cxabi.c, and type, boxing, and reflection helpers in platform/common/cxtype.c. The internal GC coordination header is platform/common/cxgc.h and is private to the runtime build.

An interface reference contains its dispatch vtable, receiver pointer, and an optional owning object. For a boxed value type, the receiver points to the boxed payload while the owner keeps the managed box available and allows casts back to object. The owner is null for ordinary compiler-created class and unboxed-struct interface references.

Version checks ​

cx.h defines CX_RUNTIME_ABI_VERSION and declares cx_runtime_abi_version() / cx_runtime_require_abi(). cxcore publishes the same number as the CMake variable CXCORE_ABI_VERSION. Generated projects require ABI 1 at C compile time and reject a different CMake runtime ABI during configuration. Generated executable entry points and dynamic module initializers also ask the loaded runtime to verify the ABI before CX code runs. This catches stale or mismatched dynamic runtimes at startup; a runtime that does not export the version-check function fails to link or load.

Versioning policy ​

The ABI version is an integer. While CX remains in early alpha and before its first release, ABI changes may continue to use version 1. Once compatibility expectations are established, changes that alter generated C layout, symbol signatures, calling conventions, type identity, or runtime behavior relied on by generated code must follow an explicit versioning policy. The compiler's generated-code requirement and cxcore's header, runtime, and CMake version must be updated together.

Milestone 11 has established a first collector design and implementation, but Milestone 16 extends it with explicit native worker attachment and cooperative collection. Native C static roots must still be registered, and modules with registered roots cannot be unloaded. Generated CX workers and System.Threading APIs now use the shared runtime and cooperative safepoints; see threading-gc-design.md. Keep the ABI experimental until the supported threading, safepoints, and native interop contracts are sufficient for a stable compatibility promise. A future stable ABI should also record architecture, compiler/toolchain, and platform constraints explicitly.

Milestone 17 extends version 1 with fixed UTF-16 wchar/WideString metadata, owned native buffers, typed C function pointers, native loaders, callback registrations and a reentrant native-call GC boundary. This remains a pre-release experimental ABI: rebuild generated code and runtime together when layouts change. SDK records use their C layout without CX headers; native functions never use managed delegate or boxing representations. Supported foreign ABIs are MSVC Windows x86/x64 and GCC/Clang Linux x64. Future stable compatibility changes must increment the version and publish platform/toolchain constraints. See native-interop-design.md for the complete contract.
